1\. Capture helpers lack docstrings 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
normalize_svg, text_rows, and inspector_elements are new public functions without Google-style
docstrings. Their accepted paths, normalization behavior, and return values must be inferred from
dense implementation details when capture comparison logic changes.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The new public capture-comparison helpers lack Google-style docstrings describing their arguments and return values. ## Fix Focus Areas - Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-09-18-mcp-inspector-guidance/current-dev/approved-closeout/lifecycle/2722-compare-captures.py[4-29] ## Recommended Fix Add a Google-style docstring to each public helper, including `Args:` and `Returns:` sections that describe the accepted path and produced normalized data. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Added Google-style Args/Returns docstrings to all three comparison helpers. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.

2\. Guidance helpers lack docstrings 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
guidance, assert_hidden, show_detail, and clear_detail are new public test helpers without
Google-style docstrings. Their inspector assumptions, accepted detail kinds, and side effects must
be reconstructed from each helper body when the test matrix changes.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The new public inspector-guidance test helpers do not have the Google-style docstrings required for public functions. ## Fix Focus Areas - Tests/UI/test_mcp_inspector_guidance.py[23-58] ## Recommended Fix Add concise Google-style docstrings to all four helpers, documenting parameters and asynchronous side effects while omitting sections that do not apply. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Added concise Google-style docs to all four guidance helpers, including the settled inspector assumptions, supported detail kinds and assertion effects. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.

3\. Probe helpers lack docstrings 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
record and probe are new public functions without Google-style docstrings. The output-writing
behavior and fixture-wide monkeypatch effects remain undocumented for later diagnostic changes.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The new public click-probe functions lack Google-style docstrings describing their arguments and effects. ## Fix Focus Areas - Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-09-18-mcp-inspector-guidance/current-dev/approved-closeout/tests/2722_click_probe.py[7-10] ## Recommended Fix Add Google-style docstrings to `record` and `probe`, including `Args:` sections and descriptions of file output and monkeypatch behavior. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Documented the JSONL event output and fixture-wide Pilot/Button patches. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.

4\. Lifecycle imports break group ordering 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
The lifecycle script places third-party portalocker directly after the standard-library pathlib
import without a blank-line separator. Future import formatting tools will rewrite this newly
committed evidence script and create avoidable artifact churn.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The new lifecycle script does not separate its standard-library and third-party imports into distinct groups. ## Fix Focus Areas - Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-09-18-mcp-inspector-guidance/current-dev/approved-closeout/lifecycle/2722-native-lifecycle.py[1-3] ## Recommended Fix Insert a blank line between `from pathlib import Path` and `import portalocker`, retaining standard-library imports before third-party imports. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Separated standard-library and third-party imports and formatted the lifecycle evidence script. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.

5\. Probe imports break group ordering 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
The click probe places third-party pytest and textual imports directly after the
standard-library pathlib import without a blank-line separator. Import formatters will alter the
committed diagnostic script whenever it is checked or reused.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The new click-probe script does not separate standard-library imports from third-party imports. ## Fix Focus Areas - Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-09-18-mcp-inspector-guidance/current-dev/approved-closeout/tests/2722_click_probe.py[1-5] ## Recommended Fix Insert a blank line after `from pathlib import Path` so `pytest` and `textual` form a separate third-party import group. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Separated standard-library and third-party imports and formatted the probe. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.

6\. Malformed probe delays crash tests 📘 Rule violation ≡ Correctness 
slow_pause converts the external PROBE_DELAY environment value directly with float() instead
of validating it through a Pydantic model. A nonnumeric or otherwise invalid delay reaches every
patched Pilot.pause call and raises before the diagnostic test can complete.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The probe consumes an environment variable through a direct float conversion without Pydantic validation, allowing malformed values to abort every patched pause. ## Fix Focus Areas - Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-09-18-mcp-inspector-guidance/current-dev/approved-closeout/tests/2722_click_probe.py[12-14] ## Recommended Fix Define a small Pydantic settings or input model with a finite, nonnegative numeric delay field, validate `PROBE_DELAY` once when the fixture starts, and pass the validated value to `asyncio.sleep`. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Removed the unnecessary environment setting. This reproduction now uses its recorded finite, nonnegative 35ms constant, so malformed external input cannot affect patched pauses. Fixed in 30a65af171. Six diagnostic cases and nine guidance cases pass; Ruff is clean. Original source/initial export hashes remain recorded with the reviewed export hashes and explicit transformation notes.
